venue: arXiv (technical report, Nanyang Technological University; no conference/journal acceptance stated as of v3)
datasets: 118 real-world AC vulnerability benchmark (CVEs, DefiHackLabs, tintinweb, SmartFix, media reports)
structure_gain: Removing the AC Context Graph (ACG, built from interprocedural slicing+PDG+call graph) drops success from 94.92% to 89.83% (-5.09pp) on the same GPT-4 model with RBAC taxonomy and validator held constant (§VII-C Table IV)
confound_note: Headline comparison (vanilla GPT-4 vs full ACFix) varies representation (ACG), retrieved knowledge (RBAC taxonomy), and agent loop (validator) simultaneously; a component-wise ablation (Table IV) isolates ACG's contribution alone by holding RBAC+validator+model fixed
stop_detail: Five categories of static grammar checks + def-use chain validation + structural-boundary compatibility checks on generated patches (§VI-B, Eqs 1-7), plus an independent validator-agent semantic check in a multi-agent-debate loop capped at 3 iterations (§VI-C)
threats_to_datum: RBAC taxonomy mining had 9.5% inter-annotator disagreement; ANTLR-based AST analysis has reduced accuracy/granularity vs IR-based approaches when source is not compilable (§V-B, §IX)

structure_gain: none reported (no raw-code-only baseline or no-CDG condition tested)
confound_note: No comparator arm exists; only the full Slither-derived Contextual-Dependency-Graph (CDG)-guided pipeline is evaluated -- no raw-code or no-pruning condition tested
stop_detail: Slither-derived Contextual Dependency Graph prunes to vulnerability-relevant elements before Chain-of-Thought prompting; multi-agent debate with an independent LLM validator plus a compilation check gates accepted patches (§2.2-§2.4, §4.2.2)
threats_to_datum: Small dataset (48 vulnerabilities), no baseline comparison against prior repair tools (SGuard, EVMPatch, SCRepair, SmartFix mentioned but not benchmarked), manual evaluation introduces subjectivity (§4 limitations)

datasets: Vul4J (140 Java files, 74 unique vulnerabilities, 25 CWE types)

key_numbers.metric: models robust to context-length (both null hypotheses accepted)
key_numbers.value: GPT-4; Mistral-7B and Mixtral-8x7B at 32,768-token context window

structure_gain: none reported (raw-text only study; no structured representation compared, only context-window truncation of raw text)
confound_note: Central comparison across ten LLMs confounds model family, parameter count (7B-70B), quantization (q5_K_M vs fp16), and context-window size (2048-32,768 tokens) simultaneously; not an isolated context ablation
stop_detail: No explicit grounding mechanism; all files are known-vulnerable by construction, and responses are manually classified Correct/Incorrect/Irrelevant with no inter-annotator agreement reported
threats_to_datum: Single Java dataset (74 vulnerabilities); reports only chi-square hypothesis outcomes, not absolute accuracy/F1; manual annotation without inter-rater reliability; confounded model/quantization/context-window design

datasets: SecVulEval (25,440 functions, 5,867 CVEs, 707 projects, 145 CWE types, 1999-2024)
structure_gain: none reported (no with-context vs without-context detection comparison performed; context is always provided, and its identification accuracy is assessed separately from detection F1)
confound_note: Models compared (Claude-3.7-Sonnet, GPT-4.1, 22B-33B open models) vary in architecture, size, and vendor with context always supplied; no controlled with/without-context arm for a fixed model
stop_detail: Multi-agent pipeline (Normalization/Planning/Context/Detection/Validation agents) with tree-sitter symbol extraction for external definitions/types/globals; manual validation of 300 samples defines correctness as exact vulnerable statement plus correct reasoning (§4.1, §5.1)
threats_to_datum: Contextual info extracted by an LLM (GPT-4.1), not fully human-verified at scale; model-size variability unexplored due to resource constraints; no repository-wide/transitive dependency context included (Appendix A)

key_numbers.metric: code size reduction via CPG-based slicing

structure_gain: none reported in main text as a same-model raw-code-vs-slice delta; Appendix C mentions an LLMxCPG-D-on-full-code (no slicing) condition but results are not detailed
confound_note: Baselines (ReGVD, VulBERTA, VulSim) differ from LLMxCPG in both representation (embeddings/graphs vs CPG-derived slice) and model architecture (GNN/BERT vs fine-tuned LLM) simultaneously; not a same-architecture ablation
stop_detail: Backward taint slicing via Joern's reachableByFlows() grounds the LLM's input in CPG-derived data/control dependencies; three security experts manually audited 50 generated CPGQL queries, Fleiss' kappa 0.6429 (§3.2, §4.3.1)
threats_to_datum: CPG cannot model runtime-dependent vulnerabilities (race conditions); accuracy drops sharply on deep nesting (>7 levels: 0.33 accuracy); imbalanced CWE representation in training data, e.g. CWE-121/122 have 1-2 samples (§4.4.2, §5)

venue: ASE 2026 (41st IEEE/ACM International Conference on Automated Software Engineering)
structure_gain: The text-only LLM (raw code snippet + nearby data-flow context, 0.915 F1) outperforms the graph-only GNN (0.886 F1) and the concatenated LLM+GNN hybrid (0.902 F1); adding graph structure does not improve over the text representation alone here
confound_note: Comparison of LLM vs GNN vs Hybrid arms confounds representation (text vs provenance-graph) with model architecture (transformer vs GNN) and fine-tuning strategy; not a same-architecture ablation. LLM is the independent, primary component (not a GNN-primary fusion) -- graph input is exclusive to the GNN, LLM sees only truncated code text
stop_detail: No cross-modal grounding; the hybrid model concatenates independently-learned LLM text embeddings and GNN provenance-graph embeddings with end-to-end backprop, no attention/alignment mechanism (§3.4)
threats_to_datum: All data from a single dynamic taint-analysis tool (NodeMedic-FINE), single ecosystem (Node.js), single vulnerability class (ACE/ACI); manual labeling of 1,239 packages introduces residual human error (§6)

structure_gain: RAG (retrieved MITRE CWE-database context) reaches 0.85 F1 vs the un-augmented base LLaMA-3.2-3B baseline's 0.67 F1 (+0.18); however RAG, SFT, and Dual-Agent each add a different, confounded mechanism atop the same base model rather than a pure representation-only swap
confound_note: RAG adds a retrieval pipeline + external CWE knowledge; SFT adds trained QLoRA adapter weights; Dual-Agent adds a second validating agent -- three distinct augmentation types compared against one shared un-augmented base model, not isolated to representation alone
stop_detail: RAG grounds responses in the MITRE CWE database via top-20-chunk retrieval + re-ranking (§III-C); the Dual-Agent's second agent audits the first agent's reasoning for logical inconsistencies and unsupported assumptions (§III-E)
threats_to_datum: Only 5 CWE categories, single proprietary enterprise codebase, 5,000 training examples; authors acknowledge the confounded design cannot isolate whether gains stem from retrieval, fine-tuning, or added inference

demote_reason: Full text confirms this is a purely qualitative solution proposal: three illustrative case studies (GGML memory-safety audit, libtiff buffer-overflow discovery, libxml2 CVE-2025-6021 patch) with no ablation, no baseline comparison, and no quantitative metrics (F1/precision/recall/success rate). Authors explicitly state in §6 that 'large-scale quantitative evaluation against benchmark datasets remains critical future work.' No quantitative result to extract (E5).

datasets: 31,165 professionally annotated vulnerability instances across 2,874+ projects, 15 blockchain platforms

key_numbers.metric: CoT vs standard few-shot prompting accuracy

structure_gain: none reported (no raw-code-only baseline for comparison; the only ablation present is CoT vs. standard few-shot prompting, +0.06 accuracy, which is unrelated to the AST-derived context itself)
confound_note: The only ablation present (CoT vs. standard few-shot prompting) varies reasoning strategy, not representation; no with/without AST-context comparison is provided, and no comparison against traditional detection tools or other LLM baselines
stop_detail: Vulnerability instances are grounded in professionally produced audit reports (CoinMarketCap, CertiK, QuantStamp, ConsenSys) matched to GitHub source via audited commit hashes; no automated static/dynamic verification of the LLM's own output
threats_to_datum: No comparison against traditional detection tools or other LLM baselines; possible overlap between few-shot example instances and test positives; no false-positive-cost analysis for real auditing workflows

datasets: PrimeVul-derived corpus (107 Joern-based testcases, 30 projects, 5 CWE categories)

key_numbers.value: 69.4% at 12,938 avg tokens vs. 74.4% at 5,973 avg tokens

structure_gain: AST+PDG reaches 83.2% curated accuracy vs. 53.5% for raw source alone (+29.7pp), with model (qwen3.6-plus), temperature, prompting/checklist structure, and 50,000-character budget held fixed across all ten representation variants (§4.2, §5.2 Table 6)
confound_note: Model, temperature, prompting structure, and character budget are held constant across representation variants; program representation is the sole varied factor (§4.2) -- this is the study's central, deliberately isolated ablation
stop_detail: Structured JSON output required with reasoning fields (sink_identified, data_source, validation_present, control_flow_analysis, pdg_dependencies); curated accuracy computed only on valid binary predictions matching expected labels (§3.5.8, §4.4)
threats_to_datum: Modest corpus (107 testcases); CWE-190 dominates (56/107) while CWE-122 and CWE-191 have only 4 and 2 cases respectively (inadequate for category-level conclusions); single-model, single-run evaluation with acknowledged prompt-serialization and few-shot-selection bias (§7)

venue: Georgia Institute of Technology Master's practicum project (not peer-reviewed)
demote_reason: Full text confirms the entire pipeline targets securing AI-generated code itself: Python code is generated from LLMSecEval prompts by a Code Generation LLM, vulnerabilities are found by CodeQL/Bandit static analyzers (not by an LLM-based representation/context mechanism as the analysis technique), and the LLM's role is generation and remediation of its own output, enriched with MITRE ATT&CK/CWE context. This is security of LLM-generated code, not use of program representations/context to drive LLM-based security analysis of arbitrary code (E4).
